text:
I’m also inviting my mom to visit us, and the process has been much more complicated than expected. Since I’m pregnant and she’s coming to help me, we wanted to make sure she wouldn’t have any issues entering Israel.

We had an appointment at Misrad Hapnim TODAY, translated documents into English, submitted copies, photos, my husband’s payslips, and paid a 105 NIS fee. In the end, they told us to wait for a decision by email, and if approved, my mom will have to collect a document from the Israeli Embassy in Peru.

Considering Peruvians don’t need a visa to enter Israel, I’m honestly not sure if this process is worth it, since it still doesn’t guarantee approval.
